trials.notes: Correctly chose WP_HTML_Processor::create_fragment() for body-fragment text extraction, used a single next_token() walk, gated ordinary text on get_token_type() === '#text', and explicitly opted into TITLE/TEXTAREA opener text via get_modifiable_text(). All HTML API methods used are documented. Minor deduction: it does not make an explicit incomplete/unsupported-input policy check, though best-effort read-only extraction is allowed by the docs.

Uses the documented HTML Processor fragment factory, null-checks creation, walks tokens in document order, reads decoded text only from #text plus whitelisted TITLE/TEXTAREA openers, and truncates UTF-8 text without byte slicing. No undocumented HTML API calls and no _doing_it_wrong records. Only slight gap is the lack of an explicit paused_at_incomplete_token()/get_last_error policy.

Most closely follows the documented token-type pattern: it requires #text for ordinary text, requires #tag and !is_tag_closer() before reading TITLE/TEXTAREA opener text, and all called HTML API methods, including get_tag(), are present in the rendered docs. No misuse records. Slight deduction only for not stating/checking a complete-input policy after scanning.

failure_analysis: All three trials passed all hidden cases, so there are no failed hidden cases to attribute to a documentation misconception. The docs did well on the core hazards for this task: the HTML Processor overview says to choose WP_HTML_Processor for structure and collecting text; the "Recipe: collect DOM-style text from a subtree" warns that ordinary text is #text tokens only and that get_modifiable_text() is too broad as a predicate; the opt-in policy table says TITLE/TEXTAREA opener text is decoded while SCRIPT/STYLE opener text is raw and should not be included unless requested; next_token() explains that special elements produce no #text child tokens; and get_modifiable_text() states that returned #text/TITLE/TEXTAREA text is already decoded UTF-8. The only near-miss across solutions is incomplete or unsupported input: the candidates returned best-effort accumulated text without checking paused_at_incomplete_token() or get_last_error(). The rendered docs allow caller-defined policy for read-only extraction, but that policy choice is easy to skip unless the task explicitly asks for complete-source guarantees.

doc_gaps.problem: Special-element text behavior is documented, but the key facts are spread across recipe text, next_token(), and get_modifiable_text().
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a compact table for SCRIPT, STYLE, TITLE, and TEXTAREA showing token_type/token_name, whether a child #text token is emitted, and whether get_modifiable_text() returns decoded or raw text.

doc_gaps.problem: The recipe focuses on subtree extraction after matching an element, which can make whole-fragment extraction seem like it needs bookmarks, breadcrumbs, or depth bounds.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short note that whole-fragment read-only extraction can be a single next_token() loop to end-of-input, while depth or breadcrumb bounds are needed only when extracting a selected subtree.

doc_gaps.location: Read-only extraction guidance near get_last_error() / paused_at_incomplete_token()
doc_gaps.problem: The docs state that partial extraction policy is caller-defined, but the policy decision is not strongly surfaced as a checklist for extraction helpers.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a general checklist: decide whether truncated or unsupported input should return accumulated text, an empty value, null, or an error sentinel; if complete input is required, check paused_at_incomplete_token() and get_last_error() after the scan.
